observation.visible_scene: A hand-modeled clay/plasticine figure shaped like an ice-cream cone stands upright near the center of a pale wood-grain tabletop. The 'scoop' is a lumpy mass of dark gray with a yellow swirl in the middle and a glossy highlight on the top dome; gray and yellow bits hang over the rim of the gray cone cup. A small dark-gray smudge sits on the table to the lower right of the cone's base. The scene is dimly and evenly lit.
visible_changes: The figure itself stays in the same position and keeps the same overall shape throughout the excerpt; no tipping, sliding, or large deformation of the cone or scoops is visible.
A small yellow mark/speck that is absent or invisible in the early frames becomes visible on the table just left of the cone's base in the later frames (around the middle-to-end of the clip).
The dark-gray smudge on the table to the right of the cone changes outline slightly over time, looking a touch more elongated/rounded toward the end.
The hanging gray drip on the right edge of the cone rim appears to lengthen marginally, and the yellow drip on the left rim stays roughly constant.
Background wood-grain lines and the figure's horizontal position shift by a few pixels between the first and last frames, consistent with a slow, slight camera drift rather than object motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the late-appearing yellow speck detached from the figure's left yellow drip or was placed there is not shown.
Whether the right-side gray smudge grew from a drip falling off the figure is not shown.
The state of the scene before t=0 and after the last frame is unknown; the excerpt may be mid-process.
No operator, tool, or cause of any change is visible.
uncertain_details: The few-pixel positional shift could be camera movement or a tiny nudge of the figure; background evidence is too weak to decide confidently.
The exact frame at which the yellow table speck first becomes distinguishable is borderline (faint in mid-clip, clearer near the end).
The apparent growth of the right gray smudge is subtle and may be a lighting/shadow artifact rather than added material.
The 'melting' look of the drips is static modeling; no actual flowing motion of material is confirmed within the clip.
